parsed.explanation: No documented trans-specific statute or targeting of trans visitors; open questions about documents, facilities, and care are not assumed exposures. But same-sex conduct is criminal under both controlling frameworks, with penalties up to three years, and camp authorities have held people on homosexuality charges without court protection. The absence of protections, conservative social climate with high identity visibility, and fragmented sovereignty make thin-data silence untrustworthy. Because the criminalisation is tangential to trans status and no gender-expression enforcement or universal facility/custody rule is documented, risk stays below severe institutional-targeting bands. Yet lack of recourse and latent criminal exposure keep it only at the lower edge of elevated risk.
